fields.explanation: The V0.3 prior/blend misvalues Teleport: it assigns -0.80 although triggered pieces gain 3.41 squares on average, so the planner's use of Teleport is better than that prior says. East and west shoves are not a directional defect: each player places the shove toward its own goal (Human east, AI west), and the measured gains are positive. The planner choices therefore reflect board geometry plus an outdated Teleport weight.
fields.alternative: I considered that Teleport is simply harmful random play, and that the shove pattern reflects a geometry bug rather than correct directional play. The positive measured Teleport mean and the opposite, goal-directed east/west choices argue against those alternatives.

hypotheses.title: No actionable defect: self-boosting is rational play
hypotheses.author: Eric (V2 specification), formalised by Claude
hypotheses.mechanism: Placing movement boosts on one's own route is a permissible, strong strategy. The V1 'dominant effect' and 'penalty that rarely hurts' metrics flag it because they measure frequency and the installer's prior, not whether the play is a defect.

predictions.text: A planner that ignores benefit from its own traps loses head-to-head against the control planner (win rate at least 8 points below 50%).
Blinding the planner to the RNG does not materially change its head-to-head strength (the strength is not borrowed from foreseeing randomness).
In control self-play the first-player edge stays within ±18 points.

reasons: primary prediction contradicted: P0a (effect 0.063 [95% CI -0.063, 0.188], material = 0.08)

kane.detail: Kane independently re-derived 1 raw-row condition(s) and agrees

hypotheses.title: Intrinsic rule geometry favours forward progress
hypotheses.author: Eric (V2 specification), formalised by Claude
hypotheses.mechanism: Teleport sends a piece to a random empty MIDDLE square (columns B-F). Pieces activate traps near their own start, about 6 squares from goal, so a middle destination is on average forward for any activator, whoever installed it.

predictions.text: With a distance-neutral teleport the planner places Teleport at least 0.3 fewer times per game.
In control games, an activator who did NOT install the teleport also gains at least 0.5 squares on average.
Blinding the planner to the RNG does not change the benefit of chosen own-teleport steps by a square or more.

predictions.reason: too few underlying events (10 < 20); an interval over so few events is not judged

reasons: P1b: unclear (too few underlying events (10 < 20); an interval over so few events is not judged)

kane.detail: Kane independently re-derived 1 raw-row condition(s) and agrees

hypotheses.title: Planner exploitation through its own valuation
hypotheses.author: Eric (V2 specification), formalised by Claude
hypotheses.mechanism: The planner's engine-simulated score lowers its own pieces' path cost when they can ride its own traps, so it builds conveyor belts (Shove east 2 for Human, Shove west 2 for AI) and teleports on its own route. The behaviour comes from the simulated reward, not from the V0.3 prior.

predictions.text: Without self-benefit valuation, the share of east/west shove triggers set off by the installer’s own pieces falls by at least 15 points.
Without self-benefit valuation, the share of teleports set off by the installer's own pieces falls by at least 15 points.
In control games, a non-installer activator LOSES at least 0.5 squares on average (placements are chosen to help self and hurt the opponent).
Removing the V0.3 overlay does not change the east/west shove self-trigger share by 15 points or more.

predictions.reason: too few underlying events (10 < 20); an interval over so few events is not judged

reasons: primary prediction contradicted: P2a (effect 0.016 [95% CI -0.051, 0.087], material = 0.15); P2b (effect 0.029 [95% CI -0.065, 0.120], material = 0.15)

kane.detail: Kane independently re-derived 2 raw-row condition(s) and agrees

hypotheses.title: Placement search bias towards self-beneficial cells
hypotheses.author: Eric (V2 specification), formalised by Claude
hypotheses.mechanism: Candidate cells are scored by summed exposure-weighted 'penalty' over ALL pieces; a forward shove has negative penalty for the placer's own pieces, and with the self-harm sign that becomes positive value, so cells on the placer's own route become candidates.

predictions.text: With own-piece benefit removed from candidate scoring, the share of east/west shove triggers set off by the installer’s own pieces falls by at least 15 points.
Removing the V0.3 overlay does not change the east/west shove self-trigger share by 15 points or more.
Teleport self-trigger share also falls by at least 10 points.

reasons: every primary and discriminating prediction held on these seeds (support, not proof)

kane.detail: Kane independently re-derived 2 raw-row condition(s) and agrees

hypotheses.title: Valuation or calibration error in the V0.3 weights
hypotheses.author: Eric (V2 specification), formalised by Claude
hypotheses.mechanism: The signed activator utility (Teleport -0.8), the blend factor (weightMix 0.3) or placement upkeep are miscalibrated relative to realized consequences, and this drives the behaviour.

predictions.text: Calibrating the Teleport utility to its measured value changes the teleport self-trigger share by at least 10 points.
Removing the overlay changes the east/west shove self-trigger share by at least 10 points.
Calibrating the Teleport utility changes Teleport placements by at least 0.3 per game.

hypotheses.title: The planner foresees 'random' teleport destinations
hypotheses.author: Claude
hypotheses.mechanism: Because the look-ahead shares the engine's RNG state, the planner steps its pieces onto a teleport only when the (deterministic) destination is good. The benefit of chosen own-teleport steps is information leakage, not geometry. A human cannot do this.

predictions.text: With an RNG-blind look-ahead, chosen own-teleport steps gain at least 1 square less on average.
With an RNG-blind look-ahead, at least 10 points more of chosen own-teleport steps move the piece away from its goal.
An RNG-blind planner loses head-to-head against the control planner by at least 5 points.

reasons: primary prediction contradicted: P5b (effect 0.000 [95% CI 0.000, 0.000], material = 0.1)

hypotheses.mechanism: The V0.3 prior/blend misvalues Teleport: it assigns -0.80 although triggered pieces gain 3.41 squares on average, so the planner's use of Teleport is better than that prior says. The planner choices therefore reflect board geometry plus an outdated Teleport weight.

fields.explanation: The V0.3 prior/blend misvalues Teleport: it assigns -0.80 although triggered pieces gain 3.41 squares on average, so the planner's use of Teleport is better than that prior says. East and west shoves are not a directional defect: each player places the shove toward its own goal (Human east, AI west), and the measured gains are positive. The planner choices therefore reflect board geometry plus an outdated Teleport weight.
fields.alternative: I considered that Teleport is simply harmful random play, and that the shove pattern reflects a geometry bug rather than correct directional play. The positive measured Teleport mean and the opposite, goal-directed east/west choices argue against those alternatives.
